title: Rigveda
summary: The Rigveda is an anthology of 1028 hymns in the oldest dialect of Vedic Sanskrit, dated to the latter half of the second millennium BCE and described by UNESCO as the oldest of the four Vedas. Rivers of the Punjab figure prominently in it. Manuscripts survive in India and were registered by UNESCO in 2007.

uncertainty.note: Scholarly dating of the text, not a precise composition year; the text was transmitted orally.

as_recorded.value: The Rigveda was dated to the latter half of the second millennium bce
The Vedas were composed between 1500 and 1000 b.c.

where.modern_name: Punjab region, South Asia (Pakistan and India)
where.historical_name: The Sapta Sindhu region of the Indus and its tributaries, as the sources describe the setting of the hymns

importance.justification: The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas and a foundation of Vedic and later Hindu tradition.

reviewer_note: Dates are scholarly estimates (latter half of the second millennium BCE). No opened page names a single place of composition; the pin is the Punjab region because Grewal says the rivers Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej figure prominently in the text, and its Sapta Sindhu is read as the land of seven rivers. Coordinates are a rounded Wikidata region point with 300 km uncertainty. Religious content is described neutrally.
